item.title: Device characterization of Si/SiGe double quantum dots using exchange oscillations in Earth's magnetic field
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Intrinsic residual nuclear spin gradients in isotopically enriched Si/SiGe drive zero-field exchange oscillations, extending singlet coherence from T2∗=1.17hinspaceext±hinspace0.02extµs to T2CPMG=74.8hinspaceext±hinspace1.8extµs with N=70 refocusing pulses.

Grade 0.530 · 2.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge Noise Spectroscopy Using Coherent Exchange Oscillations in a Singlet-Tri…” · Holly G. Stemp, Harry Hanlim Kang, Chih Hwan Yang, Gabriel D. Cutter, Frederike Brockmeyer, Patrick J. Strohbeen, Max Hays, Jeffrey A. Grover, William D. Oliver

Figure

Measured singlet return probability versus total dephasing wait time across CPMG sequences from N=0 to N=70 refocusing pulses, demonstrating coherence extension to T2CPMG=74.8hinspaceext±hinspace1.8extµs.

Asks

Can exchange-coupled semiconductor qubits be characterized at zero applied magnetic field without micromagnets, dynamic nuclear polarization, or multi-axis control calibrations?

But

Demonstrated on a single double quantum dot device; operates within the S-T0 two-spin subspace; magnetic shielding below ambient hyperfine field would require modeling T± mixing.

Tools

Si/SiGe double quantum dot · CPMG exchange pulse sequences · residual nuclear hyperfine field gradients · Earth's magnetic field operation

Abstract

Exchange-based semiconductor qubits encompass a broad family of encodings constructed from singlet- and triplet-like spin states, several of which are compatible with operation at zero applied magnetic field. Their reliable operation requires characterization of environmental noise, residual idle interactions, and exchange-dependent decay, but this characterization often relies on multi-axis control calibration or deliberately engineered magnetic-field gradients. A simpler zero-applied-field diagnostic is particularly valuable for hybrid semiconductor-superconductor systems, in which magnetic fields can degrade superconducting components. Here, we use the intrinsic magnetic-field gradient produced by residual nuclear spins in isotopically enriched Si/SiGe to implement exchange oscillations between two quantum dots as a characterization tool without a micromagnet, dynamic nuclear polarization, or prior multi-axis calibration. Using Carr-Purcell-Meiboom-Gill exchange sequences, we extend the singlet coherence from T₂^*=1.17±0.02~μs to T₂^CPMG=74.8±1.8~μs with N=70 refocusing pulses. The oscillation phase resolves residual exchange in the tens-of-kilohertz regime and enables it to be mapped across the (1,1) charge cell. These results establish intrinsic-gradient exchange oscillations as a simple, more relevant zero-field diagnostic for exchange-only and related semiconductor qubit encodings that is amenable to rapid, high-throughput device characterization.

item.title: Design and Modeling of the Charge Readout of a SiMOS Quantum Dot with a Single Electron Transistor and CryoCMOS
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Simulated QNDR1 cryoCMOS ASIC achieves SET readout gain of 34.0 MV/A (Version A) and 106.2 MV/A (Version B) with power consumption of 15.9 μW and 13.64 μW in the worst corner.

Grade 0.514 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Silicon quantum electronics” · Adam Quinn, Troy England, Andrew Li, Sharmila Mustari Nandita

Figure

Plots figure of merit, sensing current, area, power, and readout time comparing QNDR1 preamplifier versions against recent literature. Demonstrates lower power, smaller area, and improved figure of merit in simulation.

Asks

How can a single-electron transistor be DC-coupled and co-designed with cryogenic CMOS amplification circuits to scale SiMOS quantum dot readout without RF components?

Before

Best previous reported readout circuits consume up to 183 μW or require larger layout areas (Gao 2023, Westebring 2024).

But

Circuit design results are from simulation across 15 corners down to 3.8 K, not direct physical IC measurements.

Tools

Verilog-A compact modeling · 22nm FDSOI cryoPDK · Cadence Spectre · Periodic steady-state (PSS) and periodic noise (Pnoise) analysis · Rhythm Python simulation framework

Abstract

Single electron spin qubits trapped in SiMOS quantum dots are a promising technology for scaling to thousand- or million-qubit systems due to their compatibility with mature CMOS manufacturing processes. A readout system that combines a single electron transistor with a custom cryogenic CMOS amplification and digitization chain offers key advantages by avoiding the use of bulky RF components or room-temperature interconnects. We present design techniques and simulation results for an optimized qubit-SET cryoCMOS interface, culminating in the design of the QNDR1 ASIC, the first cryogenic readout ASIC designed under the Quandarum project, which targets the development of a many-channel spin qubit based detector for use in high energy physics.

item.title: Heavy-Hole--Light-Hole Mixing and Spin--Photon Coupling in Germanium Flopping-Mode Qubits
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Heavy-hole--light-hole (HH--LH) mixing enables spin--photon strong coupling via LH--LH and LH--HH transitions in flopping-mode germanium double quantum dots, outperforming standard HH--HH transitions in spin--photon figure of merit r.

Grade 0.485 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “double quantum dot exchange gates” · Jose Reina-Gálvez, Guido Burkard

Figure

Ratio r (panel a), spin--photon coupling gs,02 and decoherence rate γs,02 (panel b) plotted versus magnetic field B for the ground-to-second-excited state transition at zero detuning. Shows two peaks exceeding the strong-coupling threshold r>1, corresponding to LH--LH and LH--HH spin-flip transitions.

Asks

Does light-hole admixture produce merely quantitative corrections or open useful alternative channels for coherent cavity coupling in germanium flopping-mode qubits?

Before

HH-only flopping-mode descriptions ignore explicit LH subbands.

But

Ground-state in-plane orbitals (j=l=0) only, truncated 8-state double-dot basis, specified vertical potential well parameters (dw=18 nm, UHH=100 meV).

Tools

Luttinger--Kohn Hamiltonian · finite-well vertical confinement model · input--output theory · dressed decoherence model

Abstract

Intrinsic spin--orbit interaction in germanium provides electrically active flopping-mode qubits without requiring magnetic-field gradients to generate spin--charge hybridization. We study double quantum dots (DQDs) with a multiband Luttinger--Kohn framework that retains heavy-hole (HH) and light-hole (LH) states on equal footing. Modeling vertical confinement with a finite confinement potential along the growth direction brings selected subbands into a regime of appreciable HH--LH mixing. This admixture activates electric-dipole spin-coupling through LH--LH and LH--HH transitions, complementing the conventional HH--HH pseudospin-flip resonance. For the parameter sets considered, these additional channels can produce larger spin--photon figures of merit than the HH--HH transition. HH--LH mixing thus supplies a tunable ingredient for qubit--cavity coupling in germanium hole-spin qubits and extends the operating regimes available to circuit-QED architectures.

item.title: Localized orbitals and tunnel couplings from general confinement potentials in gate-defined quantum-dot arrays
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Numerically decomposes the eigenbasis of arbitrary multi-quantum-dot confinement Hamiltonians into localized single-dot orbital shells (s,p,d,…), computing inter-dot tunnel couplings directly as off-diagonal Hamiltonian matrix elements tijαβ.

Grade 0.480 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · Bohdan Khromets, William Chow, Jonathan Baugh

Figure

Decomposition workflow: full Hamiltonian eigenbasis and spatial quantum dot regions are projected onto localized subbases by diagonalizing overlap matrices, yielding localized orbital shells and tunnel couplings.

Asks

How to compute localized single-dot orbitals and pairwise tunnel couplings in multi-quantum-dot arrays with arbitrary, biased, or disordered confinement potentials?

But

Simulations performed for single-particle effective Hamiltonians before Coulomb interaction; assumes spatial segmentation parameter threshold λthr≈0.9.

Tools

numerical localization algorithm · overlap matrix decomposition · effective-mass single-electron Hamiltonian · watershed spatial segmentation

Abstract

Efficient simulation of dense gate-defined multi-quantum-dot arrays requires accurate and scalable modeling methods, compatible with asymmetries and imperfections of realistic voltage-controlled confinement potentials. We present a numerical localization procedure that rotates the eigenbasis of a general one-particle effective orbital Hamiltonian into s-, p-, d-, …-shells of localized orbital wavefunctions associated with individual quantum dots. The pairwise tunnel couplings between such states are computed directly as matrix elements of the Hamiltonian. We demonstrate this procedure on a 2D triangular Si-MOS triple-quantum-dot array by obtaining the voltage dependencies of the tunnel couplings and their distributions in the presence of disorder. We discuss the implications of this evaluation method on the many-body calculations, and relate it to the experimental tunnel coupling measurements.

item.title: Scalar Spin Chirality from Dissipative Pumping and Lamb Shift Precession
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Zero-flux circulating current in triangular triple quantum dots arises via an orbital Hanle effect where dissipative tunneling pumps in-plane orbital pseudospin 𝝈 and noncollinear Lamb shift 𝒉 rotates it to axial chirality rz=2(𝒉×𝝈)z/(γ2+4|𝒉|2), reversing current when 𝒉 and 𝝈 align.

Grade 0.467 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Driven coherent oscillations of a single electron spin in a quantum dot” · YuanDong Wang, JianHua Wei

Figure

Plots show the bias evolution of the normalized Lamb field 𝒉, dissipative pump 𝝈, their angular alignment sin⁡(θσ−θh), and the resulting axial chirality rz tracking circulating current reversals at alignment points V1 and V2.

Asks

How do voltage-driven circulating currents and scalar spin chirality emerge and reverse in triangular triple quantum dots at zero magnetic flux without complex hopping terms?

Before

Prior work observed bias-induced circulating currents and reversals in triple dots (e.g. Wang et al. 2024), but lacked a microscopic explanation for time-reversal-odd responses from real Hamiltonians.

But

Ground-multiplet approximation holds at low bias where w≳0.8; high-bias reversals depart due to contributions from charged/excited states outside the ground space.

Tools

Channel-restricted GKSL master equation · Hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) · Operator projection onto ground multiplet · Peierls flux derivative

Abstract

Circulating currents in triangular triple quantum dots reverse repeatedly with bias even at zero magnetic flux and for a real Hamiltonian, a phenomenon whose origin has remained unclear. We show that dissipative tunneling prepares an orbital pseudospin, while virtual charge fluctuations generate a noncollinear Lamb field that rotates it toward the chiral direction. Bias changes their relative orientation and thereby reverses the current. This reservoir-induced orbital Hanle effect converts a nonchiral orbital polarization into scalar spin chirality, which an exact ground-multiplet identity links to the circulating current. Hierarchical-equations-of-motion calculations show that the low-bias reversal survives beyond the second-order weak-coupling description, while the quadratic growth of chirality after a sudden voltage switch identifies precession. More broadly, time-reversal-odd responses can emerge in open quantum systems from the interplay between dissipative state preparation and coherent precession.

item.title: Dark state as a measurable state by a dispersive readout without a Purcell limit
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Dark mode coupled via ZZ interaction to a bright mode achieves dispersive shift comparable to bright state while maintaining effective zero coupling strength and zero Purcell loss.

Grade 0.432 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “A quantum-dot spin qubit with coherence limited by charge noise and fidelity hi…” · Wei-Chen Chien, Jyh-Yang Wang, Yen-Yu Chiang, Cheng-Chengh Huang, Lih-Chieh Hsaio, Yen-Chun Chen, Cen-Shawn Wu, Chiidong Chen, Watson Kuo

Asks

Can a quantum state achieve dispersive readout without suffering from Purcell decay?

But

Theoretical proposal relying on higher excited states to mediate dispersive shifts.

Tools

circuit quantum electrodynamics · dispersive readout · dark state engineering · higher-order perturbation theory

Abstract

It is believed that the enhancement in qubit-resonator coupling allows a better dispersive readout but introduces greater Purcell loss. In this work, we propose that a dark mode in a coupled quantum system may violate this rule by introducing the ZZ interaction between the dark and a bright mode. The dark mode may exhibit an effective zero coupling strength, and zero Purcell loss with the resonator photons. Nevertheless, the dispersive shift is almost the same as the bright state, due to the higher order perturbation introduced by the higher excited states. Such a state demonstrates the measurability without a Purcell limit in circuit quantum electrodynamics.

item.title: Interfacial Spin-to-Charge Conversion in Sputtered MoTe2 Heterostructures Probed by Spin Pumping and Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Spin-to-charge conversion and spin-torque efficiencies in Py/MoTe2 heterostructures are independent of MoTe2 thickness, proving conversion is governed by the interfacial Rashba-Edelstein effect rather than bulk spin Hall transport.

Grade 0.426 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · J. L. Costa, E. Santos, E. L. T. Francca, J. B. S. Mendes, A. Azevedo

Asks

Does charge-to-spin conversion in MoTe2 originate predominantly from the bulk or the interface?

Before

Differs from Pt heterostructures which exhibit strong bulk thickness-dependent conversion.

But

Sputtered Py/MoTe2 interfaces.

Tools

spin-pumping ferromagnetic resonance (SP-FMR) · spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) · sputtered MoTe2 heterostructures · thickness-dependent measurements · interface-separation measurements

Abstract

Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and their Weyl semimetal phases, such as MoTe₂, have attracted significant attention for spin-orbit torque applications due to their efficient charge-to-spin conversion. However, whether this conversion originates predominantly from the bulk or the interface remains unclear. Here, we investigate spin-charge interconversion in MoTe₂ using spin-pumping and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (SP-FMR and ST-FMR). Thickness-dependent measurements reveal large spin-to-charge conversion and spin-torque efficiencies that are essentially independent of MoTe₂ thickness, indicating that the conversion is predominantly governed by the Rashba-Edelstein effect at the Py/MoTe₂ interface rather than by bulk spin transport. This behavior contrasts with the characteristic thickness dependence observed in Pt heterostructures and is further supported by bidirectional SP-FMR and interface-separation measurements. Our results highlight the dominant role of the Py/MoTe₂ interface in enabling efficient spin-charge conversion and spin-orbit torques in TMD-based spintronic devices. These findings highlight the potential of sputtered MoTe₂/Py heterostructures for low-power spintronic applications, including magnetic memory and logic devices.

However, whether this conversion originates predominantly from the bulk or the interface remains unclear. Here, we investigate spin-charge interconversion in MoTe₂ using spin-pumping and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (SP-FMR and ST-FMR). Thickness-dependent measurements reveal large spin-to-charge conversion and spin-torque efficiencies that are essentially independent of MoTe₂ thickness, indicating that the conversion is predominantly governed by the Rashba-Edelstein effect at the Py/MoTe₂ interface rather than by bulk spin transport. This behavior contrasts with the characteristic thickness dependence observed in Pt heterostructures and is further supported by bidirectional SP-FMR and interface-separation measurements. Our results highlight the dominant role of the Py/MoTe₂ interface in enabling efficient spin-charge conversion and spin-orbit torques in TMD-based spintronic devices. These findings highlight the potential of sputtered MoTe₂/Py heterostructures for low-power spintronic applications, including magnetic memory and logic devices.

item.title: Probabilistic generation of two-mode binomial cat states using cross-Kerr interactions
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Protocol generates two-mode binomial cat states |psi(N,ξ)⟩ using cross-Kerr interactions, single-mode Gaussian coherent states, and heralded heterodyne measurement.

Grade 0.422 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “singlet-triplet qubit readout” · S. Zhao, A. Metelmann, S. Qvarfort

Figure

State fidelity and success probability plotted against auxiliary state amplitude $| gamma|$ for single-photon loss rates κ/ga. Shows peak fidelity at an optimal auxiliary amplitude $| gamma|$ under dissipation.

Asks

How to generate continuous-variable two-mode binomial cat states without non-Gaussian initial resource states.

Before

Existing bosonic preparation schemes required non-Gaussian initial states with fixed total excitation numbers, such as Fock or NOON states.

But

Requires gac=gbc cross-Kerr symmetry, small heterodyne acceptance region S, and open system subjected to single-photon loss.

Tools

cross-Kerr interaction · Gaussian coherent states · heralded heterodyne measurement · superconducting circuits

Abstract

Superpositions of macroscopically distinct coherent states, or cat states, are a key resource for quantum technologies. In particular, two-mode binomial cat states can give rise to exact quantum error correction in continuous-variable quantum computing. However, their preparation typically requires non-Gaussian initial states, such as Fock or NOON states, which are challenging to realize experimentally. Here, we propose a protocol to generate two-mode binomial cat states where the only requirements are Gaussian initial states in combination with heralded heterodyne measurements. Our approach utilizes cross-Kerr interactions between bosonic modes commonly realizable in superconducting circuit architectures. We show that by adjusting the input state parameters, our protocol remains robust to dissipation under realistic experimental conditions. Our work provides a practical route to realizing multinomial cat states in current experimental platforms without requiring non-Gaussian initial resources, overcoming a key limitation of existing preparation schemes.
